question: Is the Furniture category growing or shrinking?

gold_sql.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
        SELECT date_trunc('month', o.created_at) AS mon, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
        FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
        JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id
        WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' AND c.name = 'Furniture'
        GROUP BY date_trunc('month', o.created_at))
   SELECT
     (SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-12-01') AS december,
     (SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-11-01') AS november,
     round(100.0 * ((SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-12-01')
                     - (SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-11-01'))
           / NULLIF((SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-11-01'), 0), 1) AS pct_change
gold_sql.label: month_over_month

gold_sql.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
        SELECT date_trunc('month', o.created_at) AS mon, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
        FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
        JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id
        WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' AND c.name = 'Furniture'
        GROUP BY date_trunc('month', o.created_at))
   SELECT
     (SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-11-01') AS last_month,
     (SELECT AVG(units) FROM cat_month WHERE mon BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-11-01') AS trailing_6mo_avg,
     round(100.0 * ((SELECT units FROM cat_month WHERE mon = '2025-11-01')
                     - (SELECT AVG(units) FROM cat_month WHERE mon BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-11-01'))
           / NULLIF((SELECT AVG(units) FROM cat_month WHERE mon BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-11-01'), 0), 1) AS pct_change
gold_sql.label: vs_6month_average
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Last month (November) vs the trailing 6-month average (Jun-Nov 2025)

notes: Furniture: month-over-month (Dec vs Nov 2025) is sharply negative in every category in this seed data (Nov carries the Black Friday spike), while last month vs the trailing 6-month average is sharply positive for every category -- the sign of 'growing' literally flips depending on the unstated baseline
